To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the minimum, arithmetic mean and product operators can be used to construct a loading index that is useful for representing the distribution of heavy metals in Liverpool Bay.

the fuzzy integral is useful for the construction of a loading index, and that the minimum, product, arithmetic mean and maximum operators are useful for aggregating fuzzy sets representing the concentrations of metals.

(i) the fuzzy integral is useful for constructing loading indices; (ii) a set of loading index is useful for summarizing heavy metal distribution in an aquatic environment; and (iii) a set of indices is more useful than a single index.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of fuzzy set theory and fuzzy aggregation operations for environmental data analysis.
the selection of a set of fuzzy connectives for a particular purpose, in this case, the representation of a complex environmental phenomenon.
the use of fuzzy logic to represent and reason about environmental contamination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a fuzzy integral is a useful aggregation operation for constructing a loading index.
the minimum, product, arithmetic mean and maximum are the most suitable fuzzy connectives for the construction of a loading index.
the minimum and product are the most appropriate aggregation operations for the fuzzy sets representing the heavy metal contamination in Liverpool Bay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimum and product operators are the most appropriate ones to aggregate the fuzzy sets representing the concentrations of heavy metals.
the fuzzy integrals and the minimum are not useful in this context, whereas the maximum and arithmetic mean provide the best representation of heavy metal distribution in the bay.
the fuzzy aggregation operation chosen for a loading index should reflect the nature of the metal in question.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a fuzzy integral is justified when the data are not normally distributed.
a fuzzy integral is useful to aggregate fuzzy sets of metal concentrations, but the final loading indices are better represented by other fuzzy operators.
the fuzzy integral is a useful tool for aggregating fuzzy sets in the presence of a background level of pollution.
